answer_4.quote: Participants of our study were recruited from Prolific to evaluate the toxicity of online comments that are targeted at males or females
answer_4.guideline: participants were asked to review an online comment and classify its toxicity into one of the five levels: very healthy, healthy, neither, toxic, and very toxic. To minimize the ambiguity of the task, following the best practice, we provided to participants a guideline which included the definitions of different types of toxic language (e.g., profanity/obscenity, identity-based negativity, insults, threatening, personal attack); we told participants that a comment should be considered as toxic if any of these was identified in it.
